fixes.explanation: Jesus doesn't ease into this one. Matthew says He drove out all who were buying and selling there. I chase one runaway sprinkle across my counter and need a whole afternoon to recover, so I'm impressed.

A polite request would've made this a calmer story. The text says He drove out all who were buying and selling, and He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves. Matthew doesn't mention any gentle request.
Those tables did not stay standing, friend. Matthew says Jesus overturned the tables of the money changers. He also overturned the seats of those selling doves.
Right, those tables did not stay put. Matthew says He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves. I couldn't knock over a cooling rack without three apologies.
Jesus declares, "It is written: 'My house will be called a house of prayer.'" Prayer is what He says that house is meant to be. Then He says they are making it "a den of robbers."

Yes! Matthew 21:14 says the blind and the lame came to Him at the temple, and He healed them. The same passage that has Him driving out buyers and sellers has the blind and the lame coming to Him. That's quite a turn in a few verses.

Matthew says the chief priests and scribes were indignant. That's when they saw the wonders Jesus performed and the children shouting in the temple courts. Same sights, and indignant is the word Matthew gives.

He sure does. When they ask, "Do You hear what these children are saying?" Jesus answers, "Yes." Then He asks them a question of His own about what they've never read. Loud children are hard to miss, and I speak from experience with loud things in my bakery.
Jesus says, "…'From the mouths of children and infants You have ordained praise.'" The word is praise. He names children and infants as the mouths it comes from.
Jericho isn't the town in this passage. Matthew says He went out of the city to Bethany, where He spent the night. Good guess, friend.
Capernaum isn't in this scene at all. The text says Jesus went out of the city to Bethany, where He spent the night. In the morning He's returning to the city, hungry.
Matthew says Jesus found nothing on it except leaves. He was hungry when He went up to it. Leaves were all there was.
Plenty of ripe figs isn't what Matthew says. The text says Jesus found nothing on it except leaves. He was hungry when He went up to it, and leaves were all there was.
The temple is in this passage, but it's not what Jesus names here. He says, "…even if you say to this mountain, 'Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,' it will happen." The word is mountain.

Jesus really does say it. He says, "If you believe, you will receive whatever you ask for in prayer." That's a promise about believing and praying, given in answer to the disciples' question about the fig tree.
